page: Vultr voc-s-2c-16gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 1 physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 480 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and lacks a dedicated GPU.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a mixed performance profile. The server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 10%, and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, both ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the average category. Memory performance is split, with cached small-block read bandwidth scoring in the bottom 25%, while uncached large-block read and write bandwidths maintain average marks. Passmark metrics for CPU, database operations, and encryption are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

The instance exhibits notable performance bottlenecks in high-throughput scenarios. Static web serving throughput is poor, ranking in the bottom 10%, and Redis SET operations are weak. LLM inference capabilities are also limited, with text generation for a medium 7B model scoring in the poor category at 4.99 tokens per second. Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core and dedicated CPU allocation, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require extreme multi-threaded throughput. It is suitable for moderate database hosting, caching layers, and lightweight memory-intensive applications rather than high-concurrency web serving or large-scale machine learning tasks.
